title: Bound archived verdict-field strings at maxLength 32, not 64, not an enum
decided_by: owner (issue #34), ratified by 4-review panel (BA/Dev/QA/SecOps, all APPROVE_WITH_NOTES)
content: status.schema.json's events[].verdict and flags[].verdict (both bare, unbounded strings, committed to git and archived verbatim by the Librarian on every run) are capped at maxLength:32. Rationale, for reuse if a similar field needs the same call: the declared verdict vocabulary across status/peer-review/review schemas tops out at 18 characters (APPROVE_WITH_NOTES); the corpus's actual longest observed value is also 18 (same string, in flags[], not events[]). 32 was chosen as roughly 1.78x that ceiling -- enough headroom for a plausible longer SCREAMING_SNAKE token (e.g. REQUEST_CHANGES_BLOCKING at 24, APPROVE_WITH_RESERVATIONS at 25) while staying well below the length of a prose sentence, which is the actual mistake the cap exists to refuse. 64 was explicitly rejected as too generous to refuse a runaway prose string. An enum was explicitly rejected (ruled by SecOps in the original #34 discussion, not re-litigated in this pass) because these are dynamically-set lifecycle/verdict strings whose closed vocabulary already lives in sibling enum-typed fields; capping the length is the correct instrument for a field that must remain freely settable but bounded. Scope ruling worth keeping: flags[].verdict was folded into the same change as events[].verdict rather than deferred to a follow-up issue, because it is the identical field name, identical file, identical archive-verbatim exposure, and it carried the LONGER of the two observed corpus values (18 vs 15) -- deferring would have left the larger value unbounded. A structurally similar field, flags[].agent, was deliberately NOT folded in and NOT claimed as a follow-up, because it already has a closed vocabulary via panel_roles.items.enum eight lines up in the same schema, making an enum the correct instrument there instead of a length cap. This decision generalizes: prefer a length cap over an enum specifically for fields that are set dynamically from an open-ended but bounded vocabulary, and prefer an enum where a closed vocabulary already exists nearby in the same schema.
